summary: Butler County four-legged steel lookout of about 110 ft, described in a 1963 survey as on Clark National Forest land; marked removed; no site description today.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with an enclosed observation room at the top, painted aluminum
facts.status_note: Marked 'Removed' on the Central US Lookouts page, which gives no date. No source read describes the site now.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: four-legged steel tower with an enclosed observation room, painted aluminum, about 110 feet overall, owned by the U.S. government. The survey gives no build date.

evidence.supports: Butler County; agency Mark Twain National Forest (page header)
evidence.quote: Missouri Lookouts - Butler County - Mark Twain National Forest - 25N-4E-23
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1963 (VBM)

evidence.supports: Design: four-legged steel structure with an enclosed observation room at the top
evidence.quote: A 4 LEGGED STEEL STRUCTURE WITH AN ENCLOSED OBSERVATION ROOM AT THE TOP.
IT IS OWNED BY THE U.S. GOVERNMENT.

evidence.supports: Painted aluminum; overall height about 110 feet
evidence.quote: IT IS PAINTED ALUMINUM AND THE OVERALL HEIGHT IS ABOUT 110 FEET.

evidence.supports: Location: about 12 miles northwest of Poplar Bluff and 12 miles southeast of Ellsinore
evidence.quote: LOCATED ABOUT 12 MILES NORTHWEST OF POPLAR BLUFF, 12 MILES SOUTHEAST OF ELLSINORE

evidence.supports: Survey places the tower on Clark National Forest property
evidence.quote: ON THE PROPERTY OF CLARK NATIONAL FOREST

evidence.supports: Survey gives section 14 (page location code reads 25N-4E-23)
Clark National Forest combined with Mark Twain National Forest in 1973
evidence.quote: On July 1, 1973 it was administratively combined with Mark Twain National Forest

evidence.supports: Clark National Forest absorbed by Mark Twain in 1976
evidence.quote: on February 17, 1976 it was absorbed by Mark Twain

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one 1963 Coast and Geodetic Survey description and a 'Removed' label on the Central US Lookouts page. The page gives no build date, staffing, fires or removal date. The page's location code (25N-4E-23) and the survey's 'section 14' do not match; the story says so. Height 33.5 m is converted from 'about 110 feet'. The brief's coordinates (36.8093, -90.6017) were not checked against the survey's position description. The Clark National Forest merger dates come from Wikipedia, which cites its own sources; only the quoted lines were checked. The page carries a photo credited to Bob Frakes and dated February 19, 2016; the text does not say what it shows, so it is not used. Brief record: county, agency and status 'gone' match the page; ownership 'federal' matches the survey's government ownership, but ownership is not a facts key and is not recorded here.
